questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight through your lane to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your path angle may push you into another lane and cause a collision.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?
questions.explanation: Secure loads as low as possible to keep your motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in broad daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times, even during the day.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on the left. Riding on the right side may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane too quickly and unsafely.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle operators?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators must use proper eye protection when riding in Georgia.

questions.question: What feeling in your steering shows your front tire is flat?
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do about the front brake?

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip over. Use the rear brake instead to control your speed.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean do not pass. Dashed white lines mean you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black symbols give important information about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: At night, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Slow down and adjust your position in the lane as needed.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers must lean with the operator during turns and should avoid loose clothing that could catch on the motorcycle. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger on your motorcycle, you should instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers to stay still and quiet while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should board only after the engine is running. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: If wearing a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool while in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you in a crash, regardless of the weather. Jackets also protect you from dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane contains an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the lane usually has enough grip for safe riding, except when it rains. The strip is usually about two feet wide. You can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of your lane.

questions.question: The key to making a quick turn is to:

options.text: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn or avoid an obstacle, lean your motorcycle quickly in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more you need to lean.

questions.question: When being passed, it is usually best for motorcyclists to be in which part of the lane?
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May exceed the speed limit by 10 mph.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Are required to ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the speed limit when passing. Only pass another vehicle where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: _________ of all collisions between a motorcycle and a passenger vehicle are caused by drivers failing to yield the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.
questions.explanation: More than half of collisions between motorcycles and passenger vehicles happen because drivers do not yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Motorcyclists should never assume that drivers will yield, even if the law requires them to.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see the road ahead.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being hit from behind.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. You cannot see as well at night. You need more time and space to react to hazards ahead.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: Before starting out, you should make sure the fuel valve is:
questions.explanation: Before you ride, open your fuel supply valve. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines. But it will stop once those lines are empty.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center lane position when traffic allows. This position places you in the driver's rearview mirror where they are most likely to see you. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, position yourself so the driver can see you in:
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror where they will see you best. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: If you must carry a load on your motorcycle, it should be:

options.text: Carried on the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against a sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.

questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause a skid.
